text:
Anna C: quick design check — putting up a tiny mock of the escalation preview. main ask: does the routing pill copy make it clear when a message will escalate vs. when it will fallback? wondering if we need a stronger affordance for 'escalates to on-call' vs 'sends to fallback channel'. Maya: nice — can you paste the copy you used for each state? Anna C: sure. current pills: [Escalate → On‑call] and [Fallback → Ops-queue]. we also show a small lightning icon for escalate and a loop arrow for fallback. Ravi: accessibility nit — icons alone are not enough. screenreader text should announce the behavior, e.g. "Escalates to on-call with escalation policy X" vs "Sends to fallback channel: Ops-queue". otherwise AT users won't know if this triggers paging. Jordan: +1 to Ravi. Also UX question: should we expose policy name inline or hide behind a tooltip? inline is clearer but will bloat the pill. maybe truncate and offer full name on hover. Anna C: proposal: pill copy becomes "Escalates → On‑call (PagerPolicy: Primary)" but visible only when space allows; otherwise show tooltip. Thoughts? Maya: that works, but let's keep the verb first for scanability: "Escalates to: Primary on-call" and "Fallback: Ops-queue". short, action-first. Ravi: for aria, recommend explicit live region usage when preview updates. small snippet for devs: ```
Routing preview: Escalates to Primary on-call
``` Anna C: good call. also, if a route is conditional (time window/quiet hours), we should append a tiny status: "(quiet hours)" — maybe a muted color. need guidance from PM on exact text. Jordan: can we avoid parentheses? assistive tech reads punctuation oddly. maybe use em dash: "Escalates to Primary on-call — quiet hours" or a separate visually hidden label. Maya: copy polish: avoid jargon like "fallback" for some customers. use "secondary channel" in UI copy, and keep "fallback" in internal docs. Anna C: capture: change pill copy to action-first, include policy/channel name when space permits, tooltip for full name, aria-live region for updates, avoid the word "fallback" in UI. I'll update mock and push a new screenshot. Design Bot: uploaded image — https://redwood-internal/designs/esc-preview-v2.png :tada: Ravi: quick a11y check once updated — ensure contrast for muted quiet-hours label meets 4.5:1 if it's important text; if purely contextual, 3:1 may be OK but confirm with product. Anna C: noted. thanks everyone — will iterate and post new thread when I have the updated mock. :sparkles:
